links.outcome: Appropriateness of RAG chatbot responses grounded in reference documents versus general knowledge
links.effect: 32 of 44 responses cited reference documents; 30 of 32 (94%) fully appropriate, 2 partly appropriate. Of 12 general knowledge responses, 1 (8%) was inappropriate. All 16 simulated consultation responses were appropriate and sourced.
links.quote: Among the 32 sourced responses, 30 (94%) were deemed fully appropriate, with the remaining 2 (6%) being deemed partly appropriate.

links.outcome: Source attribution of chatbot answers and flagging of general-knowledge answers
links.effect: 32 of 44 (73%) responses cited reference documents and 12 (27%) were attributed to general knowledge; all 16 simulated consultation responses were sourced from the reference documents.
links.quote: Of the 44 evaluated questions, 32 (73%) responses cited reference documents, and 12 (27%) were attributed to general knowledge.

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates the accuracy and source attribution of a custom RAG-based LLM chatbot for diabetes education using expert evaluations of simulated questions, but does not test a deployment practice comparatively.
